explainedBy: Darwin sitting alone in a cramped London room sets the scene of the decision.

storyboard.claim: We open in July 1838 in a cramped, smoky London room.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darwin seated in a small room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opening scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the story in Darwin's room and year.

noVisual: no soot or grimy window in the vocabulary; the callout carries the air
explainedBy: The same room, now heavy and oppressive around Darwin.

storyboard.claim: The air is thick with industrial soot coating the windows.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darwin stays seated; his face turns uneasy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same room kept; face changes.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the soot itself is text only.

explainedBy: Darwin at his desk with the blank notebook open in front of him.

storyboard.claim: A 29-year-old Charles Darwin sits at a desk with a blank leatherbound notebook.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darwin holding the notebook.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same room; the notebook appears in his hands.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names Darwin and gives him the notebook the story turns on.

explainedBy: The notebook page splits into two columns as Darwin rules a line down the middle.

storyboard.claim: He rules a hard line straight down the middle of the page.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The two-column list page appears beside Darwin holding the notebook.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the split page draws in.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the two-column page itself.

explainedBy: The two column headings: Not Marry on the left, Marry on the right.

storyboard.claim: He heads the left column Not Marry and the right column Marry.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A two-bucket sorter labelled Not Marry | Marry.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The page's two columns now get their headings.
storyboard.addedInformation: The actual headings of his list.

explainedBy: Darwin bent worriedly over the list, tallying his future column by column.

storyboard.claim: He sits calculating his whole life item by agonizing item.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darwin slumped and worried beside the pros-and-cons page.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to Darwin, now laboring over the list.
storyboard.addedInformation: The face shows the agony of the tally.

explainedBy: Darwin the scientist at work with his magnifier: one of history's great minds.

storyboard.claim: Here is one of the greatest analytical minds in history.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darwin holding a magnifying glass, confident.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrast begins: the scientist.
storyboard.addedInformation: The magnifier marks him as a scientist.

explainedBy: Darwin points to the tree he is mapping: the evolutionary tree of life.

storyboard.claim: He is working out the mechanisms that map the evolutionary tree of life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darwin with magnifier pointing at a tree icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the tree he maps appears.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows what his genius was working on.

explainedBy: The same genius, facing his own life, is reduced to a two-column list.

storyboard.claim: Facing his most personal decision, he is reduced to a line on a page and emotional accounting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The tree gives way to the pros-and-cons page; Darwin now holds a note, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same Darwin; the tree is replaced by the list and his face falls.
storyboard.addedInformation: The swap tree -> list shows the reduction.

explainedBy: Darwin slumps over the list: paralysis at the highest stakes.

storyboard.claim: He is stuck, relying on a rudimentary tool when the stakes are highest.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darwin slumps beside the list.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; he drops the note and slumps.
storyboard.addedInformation: The slump shows the paralysis.

explainedBy: The author Steven Johnson with his book on the decisions that matter most.

storyboard.claim: Today we explore Steven Johnson's work on how we make the decisions that matter most.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Johnson holding a book.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shift from Darwin to the book's author.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the author.

explainedBy: Johnson explains that this is not the usual reading of decision science.

storyboard.claim: We look at it through a slightly unconventional lens.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Johnson talking with a knowing smile.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same author; he starts to talk.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the lens is text only.

explainedBy: The listener holding dry calculation notes, the expectation the hosts reject.

storyboard.claim: You might expect clinical probabilities, algorithms or dry decision math.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener with notes and a blank face; the phrase struck.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the author to the listener's expectation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike shows the expectation is rejected.

explainedBy: The listener swaps the dry notes for a lightbulb: imagination instead of math.

storyboard.claim: Throw that expectation out; this is a masterclass in human imagination.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same listener now holds a lightbulb, smiling.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the notes become a lightbulb and the face brightens.
storyboard.addedInformation: The swapped object shows math -> imagination.

explainedBy: The kinds of decisions at stake: ones that shape a life and a city.

storyboard.claim: The decisions that shape a human life or the geography of a city...
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sorter of the decision domains.
storyboard.onScreenText: A human life | A city's geography
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the frame to the stakes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists what these decisions shape.

explainedBy: The third domain joins: a business; these get the least deliberate thought.

storyboard.claim: ...or the course of a business get the least deliberate, imaginative thought.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The sorter gains A business.
storyboard.onScreenText: A human life | A city's geography | A business
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same sorter; one more bucket.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: 'least thought' is spoken, not drawn.

noVisual: no icon reads as intuition; a quick confident gesture is the closest
explainedBy: The listener deciding on a quick, confident gut call.

storyboard.claim: We rely on fast, intuitive gut instincts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener pointing quickly and confidently.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From what is at stake to how we decide.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the gut instinct is mostly text.

callout.text: Only two choices on the table

explainedBy: The choice shrunk to just two buckets: Option A or Option B.

storyboard.claim: We artificially narrow our choices down to Option A or Option B.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A two-bucket sorter.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The big habit named.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the narrowing to two.

explainedBy: The listener slumped under a sheet of variables he cannot hold at once.

storyboard.claim: There are too many variables to hold in working memory.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener slumped with notes in hand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Why we narrow: overload.
storyboard.addedInformation: The slump with the notes shows overload.

explainedBy: Cause and effect: too many variables lead us to shrink the choice to A or B.

storyboard.claim: So we shrink the universe to Option A or B, which brings us to the thesis.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow from variables to the binary.
storyboard.onScreenText: Too many variables | Option A or B
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The overload becomes the cause of the binary.
storyboard.addedInformation: Links the overload to the narrowing.

explainedBy: The chain ends in our worst, most catastrophic decisions.

storyboard.claim: Our absolute worst, most catastrophic decisions...
storyboard.concreteVisual: The flow gains Worst decisions.
storyboard.onScreenText: Too many variables | Option A or B | Worst decisions
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same flow; the result is added.
storyboard.addedInformation: Completes the cause -> effect chain of the thesis.

explainedBy: The listener still holding the two-option notes: the failure has already happened before he chooses.

storyboard.claim: These decisions fail long before we actually make the choice.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener worried, holding his notes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the chain back to the person living it.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the timing is carried by the callout.

explainedBy: The trap itself: accepting that only two options exist.

storyboard.claim: They fail the moment we falsely accept only two options are on the table.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The two-bucket sorter returns.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Callback to the A / B sorter.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the false frame they accept.

explainedBy: Darwin's marry / not marry list is the same two-option frame.

storyboard.claim: Marry or not? Stay or go? Buy or sell? The failure happens in the framing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darwin slumped over his two-column list.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The binary named in Darwin's own case.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the thesis back to the opening list.

explainedBy: The listener points to a fork with a third path: widening the map.

storyboard.claim: The one tool to take away: widen the map.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener pointing at the fork with a third path.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the trap to the remedy.
storyboard.addedInformation: The third path shows what widening finds.

explainedBy: The listener heads toward the wider map before choosing.

storyboard.claim: Widen the map before you choose.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same fork; the listener walks toward it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; he moves from pointing to walking.
storyboard.addedInformation: Movement shows acting on the wider map.

explainedBy: A plain road with the listener walking it worried: a two-road map walks you into a trap.

storyboard.claim: If your map has only two roads, you walk into a trap of your own making.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener walking worried along a road.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrast: the narrow map.
storyboard.addedInformation: The worried walk shows the trap.

explainedBy: A whole city is the next case of the two-road trap.

storyboard.claim: Look at a historical trap: an entire city failing to draw a bigger map.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A city icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From a person to a city.
storyboard.addedInformation: Signals the next case is a city.

explainedBy: A New York alderman walking the streets of early 1800s Manhattan.

storyboard.claim: Picture Manhattan in the early 1800s.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The period alderman walking a street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The city case begins.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places us in the period with its decision-makers.

explainedBy: Collect Pond as it was: a clean, deep freshwater pond.

storyboard.claim: Collect Pond was a pristine 60-foot-deep freshwater oasis near Manhattan's tip.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clean water icon at the shore.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The pond appears.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the pond before its decline.

noVisual: no Lenape or Dutch settlers in the cast; the pond stays and the callout names who relied on it
explainedBy: The same pond, valued by the Lenape and the Dutch.

storyboard.claim: The Lenape relied on it and the Dutch settlers revered it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The pond held.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same pond; callout names its people.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the people are text only.

noVisual: no skating action; the pond stays as the ecological heart
explainedBy: The pond as the ecological heart of lower Manhattan.

storyboard.claim: People ice skated on it; it was the ecological heart of lower Manhattan.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The pond held.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same pond; callout names its role.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: skating is text only.

explainedBy: The pond has slid halfway from pristine to foul by 1800.

storyboard.claim: By the turn of the century the smell is atrocious.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A spectrum from Pristine pond to Shocking hole, marker in the middle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The pristine pond begins to change.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the decline as a change of state.

explainedBy: Cause: unregulated tanneries on the pond's edge release toxins.

storyboard.claim: Tanneries set up along the pond, operating unregulated.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow from tanneries to toxins.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Why it declined: the cause.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the source of the pollution.

explainedBy: Effect: the tannins and hemlock poison the city's own drinking water.

storyboard.claim: They dump tannins and poisonous hemlock into their own drinking water.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The flow gains Poisoned water.
storyboard.onScreenText: Unregulated tanneries | Toxic tannins | Poisoned water
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same flow; the effect is added.
storyboard.addedInformation: Completes tanneries -> poison -> drinking water.

explainedBy: The pond's wetlands collect two kinds of waste: tannery poison and slaughterhouse carcasses.

storyboard.claim: The wetlands became a dumping ground for slaughterhouse carcasses.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sorter of what was dumped.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A second source of filth added.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the pond as a dumping ground without staging bodies.

explainedBy: The marker reaches the far end: the papers call it a shocking hole.

storyboard.claim: Newspapers call it a shocking hole.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The spectrum marker at Shocking hole.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The decline is complete.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ends the change of state.

explainedBy: The alderman facing a crisis in the growing city.

storyboard.claim: The growing city of New York faces a municipal crisis.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The alderman with the city behind him, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the pond to the council that must act.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the decision-maker in front of the problem.

callout.text: A toxic mess in the city

explainedBy: The alderman slumps at the question of what to do with the mess.

storyboard.claim: What do we do with this toxic mess in the middle of our island?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same alderman, now slumped.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; talk becomes slump.
storyboard.addedInformation: The slump shows the council at a loss.

explainedBy: The council decides flatly, without imagining anything new.

storyboard.claim: A colossal failure of imagination: the council reduced the problem...
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same alderman, blank-faced, pointing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; he decides.
storyboard.addedInformation: The blank face shows the unimaginative call.

callout.text: Leave it or get rid of it

explainedBy: The council's binary: leave it alone or get rid of it.

storyboard.claim: ...to a binary: leave it and let disease spread, or get rid of it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A two-bucket sorter with the council's options.
storyboard.onScreenText: Leave it alone | Get rid of it
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The decision named as the binary.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the council's two-option frame.

explainedBy: A third path ahead that the city did not take.

storyboard.claim: There was an alternative path that was not taken.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The fork with a third path.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the binary to the option outside it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The third path shows the missed alternative.

explainedBy: Citizens bring in L'Enfant, who arrives with his plan.

storyboard.claim: Concerned citizens brought in Pierre Charles L'Enfant, who designed Washington DC.
storyboard.concreteVisual: L'Enfant walking in with a plan in hand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The person who sees the third path.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the architect with his plan.

explainedBy: L'Enfant points to the third path the council missed.

storyboard.claim: L'Enfant did not see a binary problem.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same L'Enfant, now pointing at the fork with a third path.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; he stops and points, the third path appears.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows he sees the option beyond A or B.
